headline: Record backlog and strong profit growth on higher sales
summary_short: Revenue rose 17.2% y/y to $2,252.1M and GAAP operating income grew 35.7% to $232.5M. Backlog reached a record $33.0B and non-GAAP EPS was $4.36.
summary_long: Growth was led by ISTAR and EW (+32%) and C4I and Cyber (+11%); Aerospace rose 4%. GAAP gross margin was 25.3% versus 24.9%. Financial expenses fell to $16.3M on lower average debt, while a $27.0M pension-termination charge hit other expenses. Management cited free cash flow of $276M. A $1.00 per share dividend was declared. Management expects high-teens revenue growth and continued margin expansion in 2027.
confidence_notes: US-GAAP release (6-K). Shard EPS of $4.36 is the company's non-GAAP figure; its y/y prior in the shard ($2.88) does not match the release's $3.35, so release figures are used. The 2027 outlook is qualitative, so no numeric guidance entry was written.

drivers.explanation: ISTAR and EW rose 32% on airborne and land high power laser, electronic warfare and maritime sales in Asia-Pacific. C4I and Cyber rose 11% on command and control sales in Europe; Aerospace rose 4% on UAVs in Israel.
Gross margin widened to 25.3% from 24.9%, operating expenses fell as a share of revenue, and other operating income included a gain on sale of a US subsidiary.
The increase in backlog during the quarter came mainly from Europe; about 74% of backlog is from orders outside Israel.
Net income grew in line with activity; lower financial expenses helped, partly offset by a higher tax rate from Pillar II and a pension-plan termination expense.
